item.description:
Features:
  • Cursor usage without the tokscale CLI: Syrtis downloads your usage itself, using the Cursor app's login on this Mac. A card on the Overview asks first (only if Cursor is installed); after Continue it syncs at launch and every 30 minutes. The login goes only to cursor.com and is never saved; Syrtis stores the date, model, token counts, cost and conversation ID of each request, and turning it off deletes them. Settings -> General -> Cursor usage sync has the switch and Sync Now. If the tokscale CLI already has Cursor data, Settings asks before Syrtis uses its own sync, so usage is counted once.
Fixes:
  • Cursor usage synced by a recent tokscale CLI (saved as usage.json) is now read. Thanks @whes1015.

Fixes:
  • Syrtis kept more than half of a CPU core busy while the popover was open: the activity light redrew the whole popover up to about 120 times a second, and the popover's content ran unseen from launch. With demo data and the popover open, the main thread alone used 57.5% of one core before; the whole app now uses 2.1%. The short spike each time Syrtis rebuilds its usage totals (every Data refresh interval, or every 5 minutes while an agent is active if that is sooner) is unchanged. Thanks @miyago9267.
  • An unused Antigravity window read "Pace unavailable · invalid quota data", or started a new window on every update. It now reads "Learning reset duration" until you use it.
  • An Antigravity account on a paid Google AI plan was labeled Free. The card shows the paid plan's name, and agy's merged main card shows it too.
  • With automatic capture on, an account agy signed in to during a capture could be shown with the previous account's email.
  • An extra Claude account's window card counted usage of another configured account kept inside its folder.
  • The Grok tab now shows Grok Bot's window card when only Grok Bot is set up.
  • Switching off OpenCode under Settings -> Dashboard -> Agent limits no longer hides the other quota cards on the OpenCode tab.
  • OpenCode Go's "Rolling" window is now translated in Chinese.

Features:
  • The window card can switch between accounts. With two or more accounts with live windows (extra Claude config folders, captured Antigravity accounts), a row of account buttons switches the card's windows, curve and history; the choice is remembered. The main account's button shows its email. Window names are shorter, and button rows wrap when they do not fit.
  • Antigravity has a window card and window history. Its local usage area reads "Local usage can't be attributed to this account yet." When agy is signed in to a captured account, the main card shows that account's curve and history. Weekly and 5-hour windows draw a curve from their first reading.
Fixes:
  • With automatic capture off, capturing the account agy is using merges it into one card until agy next refreshes its sign-in, usually within an hour. Turn automatic capture on to keep it merged.
  • The Antigravity card could stay on "not logged in" after one slow agy run. A timeout is now retried after 15 minutes, and the card shows agy's own error.
  • Claude's Designs and Daily Routines windows no longer show an empty history if Anthropic reports them in its newer limits format.

Features:
  • Eight more agents are tracked: ZCode, Augment Code, Hindsight, Muse Code, Reasonix, Kimchi, Senpi and Oh My Pi. Hindsight usage appears only after you run tokscale hindsight sync from the upstream tokscale CLI. Kimi Work sessions now count toward Kimi.
  • Oh My Pi is counted on its own instead of as Pi. Its usage moves from Pi to Oh My Pi and totals stay the same, except that a record present in both ~/.pi and ~/.omp now counts once for each.
  • More Antigravity accounts, each with its own quota card labeled by email: Settings -> General -> Antigravity accounts -> "Capture current agy login". The copy is kept in this Mac's login keychain; Remove deletes only that copy. Capturing each account agy signs into automatically is off by default.
  • Less memory on scans with a warm cache: peak 329.0 to 301.9 MiB (-8.2%) for all agents on the maintainer's usage, and 88% less for Cursor alone, 32% less for Claude, 29% less for Codex. Results are the same.
Fixes:
  • Long GPT-5.4 to GPT-6 requests (input and cached input over 272K tokens) are now priced at the long-context rate for the whole request, as OpenAI bills them. On the maintainer's usage: Codex gpt-5.6-sol $5,901.37 to $6,397.37, Codex gpt-6-astra $196.53 to $320.60, Claude Code gpt-5.6-sol $355.25 to $449.17, OpenCode gpt-5.4 $79.94 to $86.29. Token counts did not change.
  • OpenRouter prices were taken from the half-price Flex tier for 32 Gemini 3.x, GPT-5.x and GPT-6.x models; they now use the listed rate, from the next price refresh. gpt-5.6-sol-pro is now priced at OpenRouter's Fast tier, twice its standard rate.
  • Kiro requests that report credits are now priced at $0.04 per credit.
  • kimi-for-coding is priced as Kimi K2.7 Code instead of K2.5, Kimi Work's k2d6-agent and k3-agent no longer take Grok 4.20's rates, and k3, k3-256k and claude-opus-41 now have a price.
  • A Pi session file that begins with a byte-order mark is now read instead of skipped.
  • Grok and Antigravity tabs now end with the window history table, like the other tabs.
  • The "Quota summary" switch under Settings' Overview cards is now translated in Chinese.

The first scan after updating takes longer if you use Kiro or Pi, while their sessions are read again.

Features:
  • Releases are signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. macOS opens a downloaded Syrtis without a Gatekeeper warning, and the Homebrew cask no longer removes the quarantine flag. Installed copies update in the app as before.
  • Each release has an installer DMG (Syrtis-2.2.0.dmg) on the release page. In-app updates and the Homebrew cask keep using the tar.gz.
  • A new animated menu bar icon, Sand shoal: sand falls onto a dune while a current carries grains away, at 24 fps in four levels set by the live token rate (50K, 300K and 1.5M tokens per minute at the default pace). Suggested on Discord by charliie.
  • Animated icons follow a new speed curve: 2 fps up to 50K tokens per minute, then a log curve to 40 fps at 3M. A pace choice under Settings -> Menubar icon scales it: Light reaches full speed at 600K, Moderate (the default) at 3M, Heavy at about 10M.
  • Setup cards at the top of the Overview cover agent tabs, the menu bar icon and text, animation pace, usage attribution, start at login and the Discord profile. Existing users see them once too; "Skip setup" answers the rest. The Discord card replaces the launch-time Discord alert and does not turn the profile on.
Fixes:
  • With no quota reading, the menu bar gauge looked like a full allowance. It is now drawn faded with a diagonal slash.
  • A reading more than 30 minutes old greyed the gauge but not the "Quota left" title; the title now turns the same grey.
  • A new Settings page, or a new tab or view in the dashboard, now starts at the top instead of keeping the previous scroll position.
  • Two Settings hints described behavior the app does not have: Data refresh and the Overview card order. The Settings hints were rewritten in plainer language.

New:
  • Brand logos for the Cline, jcode, MiMo Code, and gjc tabs, instead of a letter badge.
Improved:
  • The client-tab row now scrolls with a plain vertical mouse wheel, so a mouse without a horizontal-scroll wheel can reach every tab.
Fixes:
  • Antigravity CLI now shows the shared Antigravity quota instead of an empty or duplicate limit card.

New:
  • Tracks five more local AI coding tools: Cline, Antigravity CLI, jcode, MiMo Code, and gjc.
Improved:
  • More accurate cost and per-tool attribution across AI token usage.
  • Corrected Codex usage counts for forked and sub-agent sessions.
  • Antigravity CLI usage is now dated per turn, so the live view and daily totals reflect when each turn actually happened.
Fixes:
  • The app no longer crashes if the usage parser hits an unexpected error.
  • More reliable live usage updates, including for the newly added tools.
